The coastal town of Sonderborg in southern Denmark hosts two biogas facilities converting livestock slurry, food waste and crop residues into enough biogas to meet 100 percent of the surrounding region’s annual gas demand [Courtesy ProjectZero]By Nick ClarkPublished On 17 Nov 202617 Nov 2026
As the world seeks to cut carbon emissions to slow global warming, livestock manure is driving Denmark’s energy transition.
Pigs are big business in the Scandinavian nation, accounting for a quarter of its food exports. There are as many as 12 million breeding pigs in the country at any one time – more than double the human population, and that ratio spirals if you account for 30 million more produced for slaughter and live export every year.
Managing pig and cattle waste has long been a significant challenge. According to the Danish Agriculture and Food Council, Denmark’s pig sector annually produces more than 17 million tonnes of manure, mostly liquid slurry, emitting considerable amounts of greenhouse gas in the form of methane and nitrous oxide.
However, Denmark has been engineering a biogas boom, developing facilities to convert livestock waste into renewable natural gas to power the national grid and transport, fuel homes and make fertiliser.
In just more than a decade, the country has upscaled a handful of small biogas operations into about 150 industrial-sized plants, with up to 70 percent of the processed raw materials coming from pig and cattle manure.
Today, Denmark has Europe’s highest share of biogas in its gas grid, at about 40 percent. And this has timely benefits, given the volatile oil and gas markets caused by the conflicts in Ukraine and Iran.

The Knesset (parliament) meets as Isaac Herzog, a veteran of Israel's left-wing Labor Party, is sworn in as the state's 11th president, replacing Reuvin Rivlin, in Jerusalem, on July 7, 2020 [Gil Cohen-Magen/AFP]By Nour OdehPublished On 17 Nov 202617 Nov 2026
As soon as last month’s Israeli election results were clear, the political camp opposed to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced it would work together to elect a new Knesset speaker right away.
In Israel’s current political climate, electing the Knesset speaker is not merely a procedural matter. Many in the anti-Netanyahu bloc hope it will usher in important changes to state institutions and create a positive momentum that would reflect on efforts by Gadi Eisenkot, now the de facto leader of the opposition, to form a government without Netanyahu, his coalition partners, or their legacy. These may be over-optimistic expectations.
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3Who is Ahmad Tibi, the Arab MP elected deputy speaker of Israel’s Knesset?list 2 of 3Israeli opposition accuses Netanyahu of attempted ‘coup’list 3 of 3Will Netanyahu lose this time?end of list
A powerful position in the Knesset, the Israeli parliament, could be a strategic asset for the Netanyahu opposition.
Under the law, the Knesset speaker has the power to set the agenda of the legislature, preside over proceedings, and manage the parliamentary process under the Knesset Rules of Procedure – including convening parliament for and presiding over a vote of confidence in the government.
Eisenkot and his political allies in the so-called “Change bloc” agreed on their nominees for speaker and the chairs of key committees. The request to hold a vote to elect the speaker was filed when the 26th Knesset was sworn in...

Irish ‌‌‌‌boxer Lee Reeves has died ⁠⁠⁠⁠at the ⁠⁠⁠⁠age of 31, three months after suffering serious injuries during a bout, his boxing promotion company, Queensberry, has announced.
“Everyone at Queensberry is devastated ⁠⁠⁠⁠to learn of the ⁠⁠⁠⁠passing of Lee Reeves,” the promoters said in a statement on Tuesday.
“Lee was an immensely talented boxer, as well ⁠⁠⁠⁠as a true role model and inspiration to ⁠⁠⁠⁠his community.”
Reeves underwent surgery after his knockout loss to Gary Cully in a junior welterweight bout in August in Dublin, ‌‌‌‌and had been in a medically induced coma ever since, local media in his hometown of Limerick ⁠⁠⁠⁠said.
The reports added that he had contracted an infection over the weekend which led to his death on Monday.
Reeves won 16 of his ‌‌‌‌18 ‌‌‌‌professional bouts, including 11 by knockout.Lee Reeves, left, in action against Gary Culley in Dublin, Ireland on August 1, 2026 [Damien Eagers/Getty Images]
Cully described Reeves as “a ⁠⁠⁠⁠character and a gent”.
“We shared the ring back in August but we’ve been going back for years,” he wrote on social media.
“I still remember the stadium days when I used to watch Lee in the nationals, a weight above me, and was always impressed by his fights and his flashy gear,” Cully added.
“It’s never been nothing but love between us, champ. Can’t really believe I’m writing this, but RIP, brother.”

The bridge stretches for 19km (11.8 miles) and is also used by trains.
Reporting from Moscow, Al Jazeera’s Yulia Shapovalova said Russia came under one of the largest Ukrainian drone attacks on Monday night.
“According to official data from the Ministry of Defence, Russian air defence systems destroyed more than 1,400 drones over 23 regions, including border regions and regions in central Russia. Meanwhile, the mayor of Moscow said that more than 800 drones flew towards the capital,” Shapovalova reported.
Also on Tuesday, Moscow attacked two bridges in Kyiv, Russia’s Ministry of Defence said.
